definitions.explanation: A human individual. The basic word for referring to people in general.
Used to refer to others in general. {人|ひと}に{言|い}う (to tell someone), {人|ひと}の{話|はなし} (what others say).
The nature or personality of a person. いい{人|ひと} (a good/kind person).

examples.english: There are a lot of people, aren't there?

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}には{親切|しんせつ}な{人|ひと}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: There are many kind people in Japan.

examples.japanese: {電車|でんしゃ}の{中|なか}で{本|ほん}を{読|よ}んでいる{人|ひと}を{見|み}ると、{自分|じぶん}も{読|よ}みたくなる。
examples.english: When I see people reading books on the train, it makes me want to read too.

examples.japanese: {人|ひと}のことを{気|き}にしないで。
examples.english: Don't worry about what others think.

examples.japanese: {人|ひと}に{迷惑|めいわく}をかけてはいけません。
{人|ひと}の{話|はなし}をよく{聞|き}くことが{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: It's important to listen well to what others say.

examples.japanese: {人|ひと}の{気持|きも}ちが{分|わ}かる{人|ひと}になりたいと{思|おも}っている。
examples.english: I want to become someone who understands other people's feelings.
They're a good person, aren't they?

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{優|やさ}しい{人|ひと}だ。
あの{人|ひと}は{面白|おもしろ}い{人|ひと}です。
examples.english: That person is an interesting person.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{人|ひと}がいい。
{彼|かれ}は{仕事|しごと}ができる{人|ひと}だけど、ちょっと{厳|きび}しい{人|ひと}なので、{話|はな}しにくい。
examples.english: He's a capable person, but he's a bit strict, so he's hard to talk to.

notes: {人|ひと} has multiple readings: ひと (standalone or in some compounds), じん (nationality/occupation suffix like {日本人|にほんじん}, アメリカ{人|じん}), にん (counter for people like {三人|さんにん}). As a suffix, 〜{人|じん} often indicates nationality or a type of person.
